chief_complaint: persistent oral thrush, chronic diarrhea, and failure to thrive since birth
hpi_details: 6-month-old male infant brought in by mother for recurrent severe infections, including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP), chronic intractable diarrhea, and oral candidiasis that does not respond to antifungals. The infant has fallen off the growth curve (failure to thrive).
ideas: mother thinks the baby just has a weak stomach and needs different formula
concerns: mother is devastated because the baby is not growing and is always sick
expectations: wants a stronger antifungal for the mouth and a better formula
pmh: Multiple hospitalizations for pneumonia and sepsis
social_hx: Lives with parents, no sick contacts

investigation_events.title: Lymphocyte subset panel
investigation_events.availability_message: The lymphocyte subset panel is now available.

core_concepts: SCID is a pediatric emergency characterized by profound T-cell deficiency with markedly impaired B-cell function; circulating B-cell numbers vary by genetic subtype.
Classic presentation includes failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, and severe opportunistic infections (PJP, severe candidiasis) in the first months of life.
Live vaccines (e.g., Rotavirus) are strictly contraindicated and can cause fatal systemic infection.
Curative treatment requires hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT).
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: persistent oral thrush, chronic diarrhea, and failure to thrive since birth
Key HPI features: Infant with opportunistic infection (PJP), refractory thrush, and failure to thrive.
Objective/Exam findings: Cachectic infant. Profuse oral candidiasis. Absence of tonsils or lymph nodes on exam.
common_misconceptions: Treating recurrent severe infections in an infant simply as 'bad luck' or day-care exposure.
Administering live vaccines to infants without checking newborn screening results for SCID (TRECs).
dangerous_errors: Giving live attenuated vaccines (e.g., rotavirus, MMR) which can cause fatal vaccine-strain disease.
Transfusing non-irradiated blood products, leading to fatal Transfusion-Associated Graft-versus-Host Disease (TA-GVHD).
management_principles: Urgent referral to pediatric immunology for HSCT evaluation.
Strict avoidance of live vaccines and use ONLY irradiated, leukocyte-reduced, CMV-negative blood products.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 6-month-old male presenting with failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, refractory oral candidiasis, and a history of PJP pneumonia.
reference_soap.objective: Cachectic appearance. Severe oral thrush. Lymph nodes and tonsillar tissue absent. Lung exam reveals mild crackles.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Admit to hospital under strict protective isolation. 2. Stat Pediatric Immunology consult. 3. Check lymphocyte subsets (T, B, NK cell counts). 4. Initiate broad-spectrum antimicrobial prophylaxis. 5. DO NOT administer live vaccines. 6. Ensure any required blood products are irradiated.

learning_objectives: Recognize the classic triad of SCID: failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, and opportunistic infections
Identify the absolute contraindication of live vaccines and non-irradiated blood in SCID
Understand the urgency of HSCT referral

teaching.one_liner: A fatal pediatric immunodeficiency with profound T-cell defect causing severe opportunistic infections and failure to thrive.
red_flags: Absent lymphoid tissue on physical exam

must_ask.objective: Determine severity and chronicity of infections
must_ask.say: How many times has he been hospitalized for infections since birth?

must_ask.objective: Assess growth and failure to thrive
must_ask.say: Has he been gaining weight normally according to his pediatrician?
Has he received any live vaccines like the rotavirus vaccine recently?

history.answer: He has had non-stop watery diarrhea for months, and he just isn't growing or gaining any weight.
The diarrhea started when he was about two months old, and it has been going on continuously ever since.
He passes six to eight watery, foul-smelling stools every day, but there is no greasy sheen.
No, I have never seen any blood or mucus in his diapers.
Yes, he wakes up multiple times every night needing his diaper changed because of watery stool.
He pulls his legs up and cries before having a bowel movement, but he calms down right after passing stool.
He does not have a fever right now, and he occasionally spits up formula but does not vomit forcefully.
He drinks his formula hungrily, but his mouth always seems parched and his lips are dry.
He only drinks infant formula, and my husband and I have had no stomach issues at all.
We have not traveled anywhere, and we always prepare his bottles using boiled tap water.
He was treated with several courses of intravenous antibiotics during his recent hospital admissions for lung infections.
He has fallen completely off his growth curve and has actually lost weight over the last two months.
We tried switching him to soy and extensively hydrolyzed hypoallergenic formulas, but the diarrhea did not improve at all.
No, he has never had constipation; it has been constant loose and watery stools.
He has thick white patches all over the inside of his mouth that never clear up, but no body rashes or joint swelling.
No, he does not have excessive sweating, heat intolerance, or facial flushing.
He only wets three or four light diapers a day, makes very few tears when crying, and has become much more lethargic.
Two months ago he was in the intensive care unit with a severe lung infection called pneumocystis pneumonia, and he had a blood infection as well.
He received his birth hepatitis B shot and his two-month and four-month immunizations, including the oral rotavirus drops, after which his diarrhea became noticeably worse.
I was convinced he simply had a very sensitive stomach or an intolerance to milk protein.
I am terrified because he is wasting away, cannot fight off illnesses, and seems to be getting weaker every week.
I hope you can give him a more effective medicine for his persistent thrush and guide us on how to help him gain weight.
He has had non-stop oral thrush since his first month of life and repeated severe chest infections.
He has been hospitalized three times for severe pneumonia and sepsis, but he has never had any surgeries.
We give him nystatin oral drops four times a day for his mouth, but the white coating never goes away.
He has no known allergies to any medications or foods.
There is no family history of immune deficiencies, early infant deaths, or chronic bowel diseases.
He lives at home with both parents; neither of us smokes, drinks alcohol, or has any chronic medical conditions.
He stays at home full-time with me, and he has had no contact with anyone who was sick.
He was born full-term at forty weeks by normal vaginal delivery with a birth weight of 3.2 kilograms and had no newborn complications.
He smiles and tracks objects, but he lacks the strength to lift his head during tummy time and has become increasingly weak.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 86/52 mmHg, pulse 124 beats/min, respiratory rate 36 breaths/min, body temperature 37.0°C, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air.
A visibly cachectic, irritable infant with prominent ribs, sunken cheeks, and marked loss of subcutaneous tissue.
Current body weight is 4.8 kg, which falls well below the 3rd percentile for a 6-month-old male, indicating severe failure to thrive.
Decreased skin turgor with delayed recoil, dry skin, capillary refill time of 2 seconds, and no petechiae or purpura.
Extensive, thick white curd-like plaques over the tongue, gums, and buccal mucosa that resist scraping; tonsillar tissue is visibly absent.
No palpable anterior or posterior cervical lymph nodes, and lymphoid tissue is notably absent.
Symmetric chest expansion with mild subcostal indrawing and no palpable axillary lymphadenopathy.
Bilateral fine end-inspiratory crackles heard over both lower lung bases without wheezing.
Tachycardic regular rhythm with normal first and second heart sounds and no murmurs.
Mildly distended, protuberant abdomen with visible superficial veins and no surgical incisions.
Hyperactive, high-pitched bowel sounds present across all four quadrants.
Abdomen is soft throughout with no localized tenderness, involuntary guarding, or palpable masses.
Liver edge is palpable 1 cm below the right costal margin with a smooth edge, and the spleen is not palpable.
Normal uncircumcised male external genitalia with diffuse erythematous diaper dermatitis around the perianal area, without fissures or fistulas.
